name: Lisbon
operatingHours: Metro runs ~6:30 AM–1:00 AM daily, every ~4–12 min. No all-night metro; Carris night buses fill the gap.
fareInfo: A single Carris/Metro ticket is €1.90 (2026), loaded on a €0.50 reusable navegante occasional card; topping the card up with Zapping credit cuts a metro ride to €1.72, and tapping a contactless bank card at the gates costs €1.92. A 24-hour Carris/Metro ticket (metro, buses, trams, funiculars and Santa Justa lift) is €7.25, or €11.40 including CP suburban trains to Sintra and Cascais. The airport is on the metro at the normal fare.

lines.name: Red Line
lines.firstLast: Aeroporto → city: first ~6:30 AM, last ~1:00 AM; change at Alameda or São Sebastião. ~20 min to the centre.

sights.name: Alfama
sights.note: Lisbon's oldest quarter: a hillside maze of steep alleys, laundry-strung lanes and fado houses that survived the 1755 earthquake.
sights.hours: Open-air neighbourhood, always open; fado houses from ~8:00 PM

sights.name: Oceanário de Lisboa
sights.note: One of Europe's largest aquariums, built around a vast central tank with sharks, rays and sunfish, in Parque das Nações.

sights.name: Jerónimos Monastery
sights.note: A UNESCO-listed Manueline monastery in Belém, with a lace-like stone cloister and Vasco da Gama's tomb in the church.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–5:30 PM (last entry 5:00 PM), closed Mon; the church is free

sights.name: Castelo de São Jorge
sights.note: Moorish hilltop castle with walkable ramparts, peacocks and the widest view over the Baixa and the Tagus.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–9:00 PM Mar–Oct, 9:00 AM–6:00 PM Nov–Feb (last entry 30 min before)

sights.name: Praça do Comércio
sights.note: The grand riverside square of the rebuilt Baixa, framed by yellow arcades and the Rua Augusta Arch, whose top is a paid viewpoint.
sights.hours: Square open 24 hours; Rua Augusta Arch viewpoint ~10:00 AM–7:00 PM

sights.name: Torre de Belém
sights.note: The 16th-century fortified tower that guarded the Tagus, reopened on 27 May 2026 after a year-long restoration; entry is now in timed half-hour slots with a daily cap.
sights.hours: ~9:30 AM–5:30 PM, closed Mon; timed entry slots

sights.name: Bairro Alto
sights.note: A grid of narrow streets that is quiet by day and turns into Lisbon's busiest open-air bar scene at night.
sights.hours: Streets always open; bars busiest ~10:00 PM–2:00 AM

sights.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
sights.note: An oil magnate's collection from Egyptian antiquities to Lalique jewellery, plus the CAM modern-art centre, set in a calm garden; the Founder's Collection reopened on 18 July 2026 after renovation.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–6:00 PM, closed Tue; gardens free daily

sights.name: National Tile Museum
sights.note: Five centuries of Portuguese azulejos inside the Madre de Deus convent, including a 23-metre tiled panorama of pre-earthquake Lisbon.

sights.name: LX Factory
sights.note: A former textile works under the 25 de Abril Bridge turned into a creative quarter of bookshops, street art, cafés and Sunday markets.
sights.hours: Open daily; shops ~10:00 AM–8:00 PM, restaurants and bars later

sights.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
sights.note: The highest viewpoint in the old town, a free terrace with a sweeping panorama of the castle, the Baixa and the river; best at sunset.

sights.name: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
sights.note: A 52-metre riverside monument to Portugal's age of exploration; a lift goes up to a rooftop view over Belém.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–7:00 PM Mar–Sep; 10:00 AM–6:00 PM Oct–Feb, closed Mon

sights.name: Quake - Lisbon Earthquake Museum
sights.note: An immersive museum that recreates the 1755 earthquake, tsunami and fire with a shaking simulator and themed rooms; visits run in timed sessions of ~90 min.

sights.name: Tram 28
sights.note: The vintage yellow tram that rattles from Martim Moniz up through Graça and Alfama to Estrela; ride early to beat the queues and pickpockets.
sights.hours: ~6:00 AM–11:00 PM, every ~10–15 min; queues at Martim Moniz from late morning

sights.name: Igreja de São Roque
sights.note: A plain-fronted Jesuit church hiding one of Europe's most lavish interiors, with a gilded chapel shipped piece by piece from Rome.
sights.hours: Church ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM (from 2:00 PM Mon), free; museum next door paid

sights.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
sights.note: The 1892 Ribeira market hall, now a food hall with stalls from well-known Lisbon chefs alongside the old fish and produce market.

sights.name: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
sights.note: A free two-level garden terrace at the top of the Glória funicular, looking across to the castle; a kiosk serves drinks into the evening.

railStations.name: Lisboa Santa Apolónia
railStations.note: The riverside city terminus at the edge of Alfama: Alfa Pendular and Intercidades to Porto (~3h) and Coimbra, plus the blue Metro line.
railStations.hours: Station open ~5:00 AM–1:00 AM. Mainline trains run to individual timetables.

railStations.name: Lisboa Oriente
railStations.note: Calatrava-designed hub in Parque das Nações: every Porto and Coimbra train calls here, plus trains to the Algarve (Faro), long-distance buses and the red Metro line, one stop from the airport.
railStations.hours: Station open ~5:00 AM–1:30 AM. Mainline trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport
airports.transitNote: Metro red line (shown on map) from Aeroporto station at Terminal 1: ~20 min to Saldanha, ~25 min to Baixa-Chiado changing at Alameda (green line) or São Sebastião (blue). Normal metro fare. Terminal 2 (low-cost) is linked by a free shuttle bus.
airports.hours: Red line: first ~6:30 AM, last ~1:00 AM. Late arrivals: taxi/ride-hail (~15–20 min to the centre).
